> Very much algebra. Teaching how to use Lagrangian, or how to solve driven, damped, and damped driven harmonic oscillations to a good extent. 

>However, it does not give enough intuition about phase space and Hamiltonian topics. It feels like we do many calculations, but the overall picture is never fully clear. It is fine for the course to stay within classical physics, but even within that scope, the explanations feel incomplete.

Stronger connections between phase space, complex analysis, and more rigorous mathematical tools in classical physics would be helpful. I am not sure how this can fit into the current schedule. One option might be to spend slightly less time on oscillations, although that is also an important topic.

* A more practical solution could be to briefly introduce these ideas in class and, more importantly, suggest additional readings. Even a small emphasis, combined with recommended resources, could help build a deeper understanding of the algebra we use. Overall, the course feels weak in explaining the purpose behind the algebra and what it is trying to achieve physically.

# 

Engineering physics plays a vital role in enabling flight and automotive transportation. However, viewing physics as merely calculations and clever algorithmic tricks undermines its depth. The common perception that Newtonian mechanics is straightforward and lacks philosophical richness does a disservice to students' intellectual growth. This misconception needs correction. In laboratory settings, students should progress naturally from understanding measurement devices to undermine Aristotelian intuitions recreating Galileo's experiments and deriving Newton's laws firsthand. Theoretical courses should also explore deeper questions: the implications of Newton's mathematical approach, the significance of expressing science mathematically, the origins of natural philosophy, Newton's theological arguments, scientific thinking and the fundamental principles and methodology of natural sciences. We should examine core questions: How science works? What is physics as a science? How does it relate to other sciences? What is the importancy of picture of atomic concept? If all masses attract each other, what prevents universal collapse? What was Newton's proposed solution, and what criticisms did it face? While satisfactory for engineering purposes, the course lacks sufficient depth to fully explore these fundamental concepts and does not address important concepts like buoyant force, the work of Archimedes, and Torricelli's contributions.

Dear Sevinçli approached the course respectful to us and maintained English as the language of instruction, which we appreciated. However, there were several challenges in the teaching approach that impacted our learning experience. The lessons often assumed prior knowledge of advanced topics, such as differential equations, which many of us had not yet studied. This made it difficult to grasp concepts like Oscillations fully, as the material was presented in a way that required background knowledge we did not have, and our instructor did not explain the usage of differential equations. Punctuality was occasionally an issue, with classes starting 5–10 minutes late at times. Quizzes were introduced quickly, sometimes before we had a solid understanding of the topics. The questions often felt either overly basic or not closely aligned with the depth of the course content, which limited their value as a learning tool. While using an iPad as a teaching tool was innovative, the pace at which content was presented made it challenging to follow along and take notes effectively. Additionally, there were occasional mistakes in the explanations, and students sometimes had to step in to clarify points. This, combined with the lack of detailed descriptions for some equations and concepts, meant that much of the learning had to be done independently outside class. While the respectfulness and English-only teaching environment were appreciated, a more structured and foundational approach to the material would greatly enhance the learning experience.

The course was fundamental and necessary, providing essential knowledge for understanding key concepts. However, at times, topics were introduced with the assumption that we had prior knowledge, which was not always the case. For instance, in the Oscillations section, differential equations were used extensively, but we had no prior exposure to them. Clearer explanations and instructions on these advanced topics would have greatly enhanced our understanding, especially since many of us were unsure of what we were doing.
The lab sessions, on the other hand, were valuable, as the experiments effectively demonstrated the concepts we learned in class. However, the lab project proved to be a significant challenge for me. I received no feedback on my proposal, and even after reaching out to the assistant for guidance, the responses lacked the clarity needed to address my concerns. This ultimately resulted in a poor outcome for my project. Moreover, the lab assistants were not as supportive as they could have been during project development. For the first experiment, many of us were unsure about what was expected in our reports, leading to low grades. Providing more detailed instructions and foresight about the expectations for experiments and reports would have made the lab sessions far more effective and less frustrating. Overall, while the course and lab sessions had their strengths, more clarity and guidance both in class and in the labs would greatly improve the learning experience.

Fakat şunu diyebilirim ki derslerde işlenen konular ve çözülen sorular, midterm ve quizlerde çıkan soruların yanında oldukça yüzeysel ve basit kalıyor. PHYS101 gibi zor ve katalog bir derste puan toplamak için quizler kesinlikle çok büyük bir avantaj fakat Haldun hocanın hazırladığı quizler gerçekten çok zor ve 100 almak neredeyse imkansız. Onun haricinde haftalık quizlerin yapılmasını doğru buluyorum çünkü ister istemez öğrenci her hafta işlenen konulara quizden önce baktığından dolayı öğrenci dersi takip edebiliyor.

Lab asistanının, bugüne kadar gördüğüm en deneyimsiz ve bu üniversitenin standartlarına yakışmayan bir eğitmen olduğunu düşünüyorum. Süreç, ilk 'proposal'ımızı (öneri raporu) gönderdiğimizde başladı; asistan, tüm sınıfın geri bildirimlerini tatilin son günü paylaştı ve sınıfın yarısının raporunu reddetti. Final versiyonunu hazırlamak için sadece iki günümüz kalmıştı ve birçok arkadaşım sıfırdan başlamak zorunda bırakıldı.

Kendi deneyimimden bahsetmek gerekirse; 4 yıl önce asistanlık (TA) yapmış tecrübeli bir arkadaşıma raporumu inceletmiştim. Kendisi, raporun derse uygun olduğunu ve yüksek not alacağını öngörmüştü; ancak buna rağmen benim 'proposal'ım da reddedildi. Nedenini öğrenmek için yanına gittiğimde, raporumu dikkatli okumadığını fark ettim (eksik olduğunu iddia ettiği kısımlar raporda mevcuttu). Bu durum bende büyük bir hayal kırıklığı yarattı. Yine de kısıtlı sürede, büyük bir stres altında raporu sıfırdan hazırlamak zorunda kaldım.

Deney esnasında da kendisi oldukça yetersizdi; sorularımın hiçbirine tatmin edici veya doğru bir cevap alamadım. Sık sık konuyu kendisinin de bilmediğini belirtmesi, laboratuvardaki herkesin güvenini ve motivasyonunu kırdı. Özetle, laboratuvar asistanının yetkinliğinin bu üniversite için yetersiz olduğunu ve Fizik 101 laboratuvar sürecimin son derece verimsiz geçmesine neden olduğunu belirtmek isterim. 

Bu üniversitede böyle insanları barındırması sadece ismini lekeliyor. Daha çok yazılcak şey var fakat karakter sınırı mevcut. Anlatabildiklerim bu kadar.

The course was very dull. Most of the time, the professor just came into class and filled the board with equations from his notes. I couldn't tell if he was explaining concepts in a way that everyone could understand. Instead, he just transcribed notes directly from the book; they looked like exact copies of the text. I really thought I could grasp the physics from this important course (and I had huge expectations for it), but instead, I think we got lost in the mathematics. While this course cannot be separated from its math and quantum mechanics, we lost track of the underlying physics. The book was also unhelpful since it skips many steps; you can't understand how it derives the final equations or which theorems were used. If you are even a little unsure of your quantum mechanics or mathematics knowledge, do not take this course. Alternatively, choose another instructor (if possible) who focuses more on the meaning of the subjects rather than just writing down mathematical equations and Hamiltonians.
